extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing disciplinary proceedings, settlement approval, and sanctions for practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO. Includes applicable regulatory authorities, examples of misconduct (failure to respond to disciplinary demands), and the types/notification of sanctions imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent ... has been registered as an attorney to practice before the USPTO and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners are governed by the USPTO disciplinary regulations; the Final Order treats these rules as the operative professional- responsibility standards for conduct before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond to lawful demands from admissions or disciplinary authorities (Va. Rule 8.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Virginia State Bar District Committee found that Respondent violated Rule 8.1(c) of the Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct by failing to respond to a lawful demand for information from an admissions or disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to respond to a summons or charge of misconduct from a disciplinary or admissions authority is itself misconduct and may be the basis for state and USPTO discipline (illustrated by the state public reprimand and subsequent USPTO action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the stipulated facts, Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, specifically 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct leading to state discipline (e.g., failure to respond to disciplinary inquiries) may constitute violations of specific USPTO disciplinary provisions; such violations can support USPTO-imposed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a Proposed Settlement Agreement (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint. The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves the disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed settlement must include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and must meet the § 11.26 regulatory requirements to be approved by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director's jurisdiction and authority to approve settlements (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter and the authority to approve the Proposed Settlement Agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements and final disciplinary orders are subject to the Director's statutory and regulatory authority; practitioners should recognize the Director's role in approving OED settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as an available sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public reprimand is an express sanction that the USPTO may impose (here, by agreement); the Final Order announces and records the reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary decisions are published by OED in its Reading Room for public access; publication is part of the sanctioning/ transparency process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette: [text of Notice of Reprimand concerning respondent and basis for discipline].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the OED Reading Room, the Office may publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the reprimand and the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO discipline will be communicated to relevant state disciplinary authorities and courts as required by § 11.59; this ensures inter-jurisdictional notice of practitioner discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings (aggravation and rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding... when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct... and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's settled disciplinary record may be used later as aggravation or to rebut mitigation; settlement does not shield against future consequences of the same conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements may specify cost allocation (here, each party bears its own costs); cost allocation is a negotiable element of settlement agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State bar discipline as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office has publicly reprimanded Mr. Brown for violating 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) based on his being publicly reprimanded by the Virginia State Bar for failing to respond to a lawful demand for information from an admissions or disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse findings or sanctions by a state bar (e.g., public reprimand, probation) can serve as the factual and legal foundation for USPTO disciplinary action against a registered patent practitioner.
